entries.reason: ASHIFT_DEBUG is #undef'd near the top of ashift.c, and the only unlocked reads of g->buf_hash are the printf() arguments inside the two compiled-out blocks in _do_get_structure_auto().  The live hash comparison that would consume it is commented out ('if(g->buf /* && hash != g->buf_hash */)' in both process() and process_cl()), so no enabled code reads the field across threads.  #21918 quotes that commented-out line but does not report buf_hash as a defect.  Re-check if ASHIFT_DEBUG is ever enabled by default or the comparison is restored.

GUI-only region-selection state sitting inside a critical section taken for a pipe-shared neighbour.  Every site is on the GTK main thread: _turn_select_region_off() is reached only from gui_changed(), _color_picker_callback(), _auto_levels_callback(), button_pressed() and gui_focus(), and the rest are framework GUI callbacks -- mouse_moved(), button_released(), button_pressed(), gui_post_expose(), gui_update(), change_image() -- with the locked sites all in _select_region_toggled_callback().  No pipe callback mentions the five fields: process() and process_cl() read box_cood and call_auto_exposure, which is why critical sections exist in this file at all (in _auto_levels_callback() and _develop_ui_pipe_finished_callback()), and the five are the GTK-side inputs that button_released() folds into box_cood.  Two GTK-thread sites cannot race.  The genuine defect on the same path -- button_released() writing box_cood and call_auto_exposure unlocked and then treating dt_dev_reprocess_all() as a barrier -- is a different field, is already reported under no_lock_share, and is filed as #22120.  Re-check if any of the five gains a reader in process(), process_cl() or commit_params().

Same ownership-token argument as the accepted rgblevels:params entry, and basicadj is a copy of that code.  Exclusive ownership of g->params passes through the call_auto_exposure state machine, and every handover is under gui_lock even though the payload accesses are not: the pipe writes params only after taking 1 -> -1 in process() and process_cl(), publishes 2 in the same functions, and _develop_ui_pipe_finished_callback() reads params only after taking 2 -> -1.  Only one preview pipe runs at a time -- dt_pipe_is_preview() matches DT_DEV_PIXELPIPE_PREVIEW only, not the distinct DT_DEV_PIXELPIPE_PREVIEW2 bit (both in src/develop/pixelpipe.h) -- so two pipe writers cannot overlap, and the two GTK entry points cannot interleave with each other.  The unlocked GTK token write in button_released() can lose a request or a result -- that is the separate box_cood/call_auto_exposure defect, #22120 -- but it cannot produce a concurrent params writer.  Re-check if the token protocol changes or a second pipe gains this path.

Colour-checker interaction state, false positive for two independent reasons.  (1) Every access is on the GTK main thread -- mouse_moved(), button_pressed(), button_released(), gui_post_expose(), and _dt_active_images_callback(), the DT_SIGNAL_ACTIVE_IMAGES_CHANGE handler connected in gui_init(), which runs on the main context like every darktable signal handler (dt_control_signal_raise() in src/control/signal.c) -- and process(), process_cl() and commit_params() mention none of the five fields.  (2) The sites the scan reports as unlocked inside _update_bounding_box() and _init_bounding_box() in fact run with gui_lock held by their caller; lock depth is computed lexically per function, so this is a limitation of the extractor rather than a discipline gap.  All six call sites are inside critical sections: in mouse_moved(), button_pressed(), button_released(), _checker_changed_callback() and _start_profiling_callback(), plus the one where _init_bounding_box() calls _update_bounding_box() and inherits its caller's lock.  Those sections exist to make the writes to g->homography and g->inverse_homography in _update_bounding_box() atomic against the preview pipe, which reads them in _extract_patches() under the same lock when called from process() (the unlocked _validate_color_checker() route in process() is the separate homography finding); the five fields here merely sit inside them.  is_cursor_close is additionally written and read in mouse_moved() outside that section, which is harmless because mouse_moved() is its only writer and the only thread involved.  Re-check if any of the five gains a pipe-side reader, or if a bounding-box call site loses its caller lock.

Every runtime access is under gui_lock.  The three sites the scan reports as unlocked -- the reads of histogram_valid and hue_histogram and the write of auto_detect_pending in _auto_detect_callback() -- are on the fall-through path of the critical section that function opens before them and closes after them.  Its early-exit branch leaves the section and returns, and lock depth is tracked lexically, so the scan counts the lock as released for the rest of the function: a documented limit of the extractor, not a discipline gap.  Every other access takes the same lock: the preview-pipe publish in _update_histogram() (reached from process() and process_cl(), and only for the preview pipe), the idle consumer _auto_detect_button_enable_idle(), gui_update(), change_image() and gui_cleanup(); the gui_init() writes precede any pipe run.  Re-check if _auto_detect_callback's early return is restructured, or if any of the three gains an access outside gui_lock.

Not shared.  The three fields are the full-pipe luminance cache, and every runtime access is in _full_preview_buffer(), whose only callers are toneeq_process() and process_cl().  Both call it only inside a dt_pipe_is_full(piece->pipe) branch nested in the self->dev->gui_attached guard, and both with gui_lock held; the helper's comment states the intent.  Only one full pipe exists per GUI-attached dev, and its worker is serialised by the pipe mutex, so the helper's free/realloc has no concurrent peer.  Every other full-type pipe in the process fails one of the two guards.  preview2 is a distinct type bit (DT_DEV_PIXELPIPE_PREVIEW2 in src/develop/pixelpipe.h) that dt_pipe_is_full() does not match.  dt_dev_image() in src/develop/develop.c builds a private dt_develop_t with gui_attached = FALSE.  The pinned second-window develop context does own a real FULL pipe (dt_dev_pixelpipe_init() in _alloc_pinned_dev()), but _alloc_pinned_dev() creates it with dt_dev_init(pinned_dev, FALSE), and its modules come from _clone_module(), which callocs a fresh module and never runs gui_init() -- so that context has neither gui_attached nor gui_data.  The two GTK sites are lifecycle only: gui_cache_init(), reached solely from gui_init(), and the gui_cleanup() free.  That teardown free racing a running pipe is the module-destruction problem reported as #21891 (closed), not a field-sharing defect.  Re-check if a GTK runtime consumer of the buffer appears, or if a second full-type pipe on a gui_attached dev becomes possible.

Three GUI-only scalars inside a critical section that exists for a pipe-shared neighbour.  The writers are the bar handlers only -- dt_iop_zonesystem_bar_leave_notify() and dt_iop_zonesystem_bar_motion_notify() -- the readers are in dt_iop_zonesystem_preview_draw(), a GTK draw handler, and gui_init() writes them.  The section in dt_iop_zonesystem_preview_draw() is held for g->in_preview_buffer and g->out_preview_buffer, which process_common_setup() reallocates from a preview-pipe thread.  Not this finding, but in the same function: image is allocated inside the section for 4 * g->preview_width * g->preview_height bytes, the lock is released, and both dimensions are re-read outside it for the cairo surface, so a preview that grows in between makes cairo read past the block.  That one is already reported by the tool under violation for preview_width/preview_height and is filed as #21916.  Re-check if any of the three scalars gains a pipe-side access.
